newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African June CPI falls to nine-month low.
newsitem.headline: South African June CPI falls to nine-month low.

text.p: South Africa's annual consumer price inflation rate fell to a nine-month low of 8.8 percent in June, beating economists' expectations and going some way to offset poor private sector credit extension.
The monthly increase was 0.3 percent with food price increases contributing 0.1 percent of a point, housing 0.1, furniture and equipment 0.1, transport -0.1 and "other" items 0.1.
Economists had forecast a 0.5 percent month-on-month rise and 9.1 percent year-on-year.

Tony Twine, economist at consultancy Econometrix, said the inflation data was clearly a good signal for a rate cut in the weeks ahead, but added it did not fully cancel out the impact of the poor credit data.
"Looking at M3 and CPI together it definitely looks like the rate cut could come in the next four weeks. But together, they don't cancel out the poor credit growth number," he said.

Year-on-year M3 grew 12.79 percent in June from a revised 15.32 in May, well below expectations of 14.44 percent. But private credit dipped only marginally to 16.39 percent from 16.65 in May, against the consensus expectation of 15.19 percent.
"I doubt that we will see a rate cut until the next credit figure becomes available and that will have to be much lower than last night's," Twine said.

Anastasia Gekis at ABN Amro said she expected Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals to hold his hand on a rate cut until seeing July money supply figures in a month's time, despite the encouraging inflation figure.

"Given the Reserve Bank's strict monetary policy approach I think private sector credit growth still plays a role and I think they will definitely wait until the July figures to decide what will happen with the rate cut," she said.
"The CPI is definitely a positive indication. It does add to the pros that an interest rate cut is likely but it doesn't negate (credit growth)."

South African long bonds took some heart from June CPI with the yield on the benchmark R150 easing back to 14.10 percent from a morning high of 14.18, though this was still above Monday's local closing rate of 14.01.
